title: Buddy Bolden-era bands: Warner Reed and Tatee, Bob Woodley
summary: Glass recalls the older bands such as Warner and Tate's, with brothers on bass and banjo, and Bob Woodley, before his time.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: But guys, Buddy Bowling, did you ever hear him? I heard Buddy Bowling.

That was an old band. I thought I heard Buddy Bowling, but you see, fuck you, motherfucker. I heard all that. Yeah, I didn't know them. Them was all old men, you see. Them men way before my time. I was coming up. I was about that size when Buddy Bowling and them was playing. They had a band, Warner in them, Warner Reed.
Warner Reed and Tatee. There was two brothers. They played bass. One played bass and one played banjo. Warner played which? One played bass and one played banjo.
Well Warner played bass and Tatee played the banjo. And we had Bob Woodley.

Bob was a little short dumb fella. Bob used to play ghetto. We called him Bob Woodley. I never heard of him before. I don't know a thing about him. Yeah. Bob Woodley. Was he? Yeah, he was good. Did he have his own band, Bob Woodley? No. Bob Woodley and them used to work with Juan in them.
You know. He used to work with Juan in them. He used to work with me.
For me. For me. For me.
For me. For me. For me. He used to call it Tate and Warner's band.
Who was that violin player? Wasn't that violin player named Tate? No. Sales? I'm going to come over here and see you. What about Buddy Lock? Did you ever hear Buddy Lock?
I thought that was a bass button. Let me see, who else I was going to ask you about? Those bands like Warner and Tate.
Them were supposed to be big bands. They were supposed to be the best bands coming up in that time. How many pieces? They'd have four pieces.
